newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate OKs Los Angeles County breakup study.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate OKs Los Angeles County breakup study.

text.p: California's Senate on Thursday approved a bill that could lead to the breakup of Los Angeles County.
The bill would create a local agency called the Los Angeles County Division Commission to study proposals to divide up the county. The commission would issue its report to lawmakers by January 2001.
The Senate voted 23-to-11 to approve the bill, by Republican Assemblyman George Runner. The bill now returns to the Assembly for a vote on Senate amendments.
In recent years state lawmakers have been debating bills to break up Los Angeles County, which has a population of more than nine million people.
